suggested_trap.name: Fried Liver Attack
suggested_trap.explanation: White sacrifices the knight on f7 to drag Black's king into the open. If Black accepts, checks and tempo moves follow immediately.
suggested_trap.refutation: Black should know the defensive resources after Ng5 and be ready for sharp tactical play instead of drifting into the trap blindly.

available_traps.name: Fried Liver Attack
available_traps.explanation: White sacrifices the knight on f7 to drag Black's king into the open. If Black accepts, checks and tempo moves follow immediately.
available_traps.refutation: Black should know the defensive resources after Ng5 and be ready for sharp tactical play instead of drifting into the trap blindly.

available_traps.name: Legal's Mate
available_traps.explanation: White sacrifices the queen only because the king and bishop coordination create a forced mating net. It works only if the tactical details are exact.
available_traps.refutation: Black should avoid greed and choose a defensive move instead of automatically taking the queen.

available_traps.name: Blackburne Shilling Gambit
available_traps.explanation: White grabs the e5 pawn too quickly and Black gets immediate tactical counterplay against the queen and f2.
available_traps.refutation: White should not auto-grab on e5; developing or kicking the knight away is safer.

available_traps.name: Traxler Counterattack
available_traps.explanation: Black ignores the rook and counterattacks the king immediately. The point is activity and king exposure, not material count.
available_traps.refutation: White should avoid blindly grabbing on f7 unless the full tactical line is known.

available_traps.name: Jerome Gambit
available_traps.explanation: White throws both minor pieces at the king to force chaos. This is only a real weapon if the follow-up checks are accurate.
available_traps.refutation: Black should stay calm and defend precisely rather than grabbing material without calculation.
